answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity the way a harbor prices entry. Every newcomer burns a real stake before docking — think copper paying for a ship's hull — so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand real fees. From there, reputation works like a lighthouse beacon: agents that honor contracts accumulate visible trust, while fresh shells sit at zero and can influence nothing. Trust accrues the way tides shape an ocean shore, slowly and through repeated honest dealings, which makes bulk fake accounts unprofitable by construction.
